# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

The bomb currently shows display `0`, a white light, and three wires in this order: green, red, blue. I’m telling the Blind so they can combine these observations with the manual and their tactile inspection. The Mute’s long gesture sequence appears to be encoded instructions, but its encoding is not yet clear from the visible symbols alone.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Visual state: display 0. Indicator light is white. Wires, left to right: wire 1 green, wire 2 red, wire 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, white light, and wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Please relay the manual's relevant procedure to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The display remains `0` and the wire colors are unchanged, but the indicator has changed from white to yellow. I’m updating both teammates so the Blind can act according to the manual and the Mute can account for the changed light state.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display remains 0; light is now yellow. Wires remain 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display remains 0; light changed to yellow. Wires remain 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Please relay any applicable manual instruction to Blind.")
wait()
```

The light has progressed white → yellow → orange while the display stays `0` and all three wire colors remain unchanged. I cannot safely infer the required action from the Mute’s gesture code, so I’m relaying the urgent visual state and asking the Mute to provide a clearer manual encoding.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Urgent update: light progression was white, then yellow, now orange. Display stays 0. Wires remain 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. I have not identified the Mute's gesture encoding; do not act on wire colors alone.")
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot reliably decode the long unary gesture message. Please send the manual instruction using a simpler agreed format, such as one gesture group per wire/action, and indicate clearly which wire Blind must manipulate.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝]

The light has advanced to purple; the display and wire colors are unchanged. The Mute’s new short code is `🖐 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝`, which appears to encode `5` followed by `3` if the hand symbols are numeric markers, but its exact meaning is uncertain. I’m relaying both the raw code and the visual state to the Blind rather than risking an unsupported wire action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current visual state: display 0, light purple, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent gestures: hand-five, separator, three pointing-up symbols: [🖐 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝]. This may encode 5, 3; interpret with the manual before acting.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐", "👌", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝]

The light has now changed to red, with display `0` and wires still green, red, blue. The Mute sent `[🤜 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝]`; I cannot safely assign a meaning to that code without the manual’s encoding. I’m passing the exact signal and current state to the Blind, who must determine the physical action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0; light is red; wire 1 green, wire 2 red, wire 3 blue. Mute's latest gesture code is [🤜 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝]. I cannot safely decode its meaning; use the manual and your tactile information before acting.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝]

The light has reset to white; the display and wires are unchanged. The Mute repeated `[🤜 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝]`, so this is likely a fixed instruction rather than a report of the current light. I cannot establish what `🤜` means, but the trailing three pointing gestures may identify wire 3; the Blind must verify that against the manual and touch-based state before acting.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light white, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute again sent [🤜, 👌, ☝, ☝, ☝]. This repeated code may be an instruction involving 3, possibly wire 3, but 🤜 is undecoded; verify with the manual and tactile state before acting.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

The light has moved from white to yellow again; the display remains `0`, and the wires remain green, red, blue. The Mute’s new signal is simply three pointing-up gestures, most naturally indicating `3`. I’m relaying that as a possible wire number, while warning the Blind to confirm the required operation from the manual.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent exactly [☝ ☝ ☝], likely number 3. Confirm from the manual whether this identifies wire 3 and what operation is required.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received [☝ ☝ ☝] as likely 3. Please encode the required operation as well, not only the number.")
wait()
```
